facts.value: Fat is an essential nutrient for proper functioning of cells in the body.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Linoleic acid and α-linolenic acid can only be obtained from the diet.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: A minimum of 15% of the energy consumed per day should be from fat.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Limiting the amount of total fat in the diet to 30% or less of total daily energy intake may help to prevent unhealthy weight gain in the adult population.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Children have unique energy requirements for optimal growth and development throughout childhood and adolescence, therefore higher total fat intakes may also be acceptable.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: The quality of dietary fat is important.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Unsaturated fat is preferable to saturated fat and trans fat of all kinds.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Unsaturated fat is found in fish, avocado and nuts, and in sunflower, soybean, canola and olive oils.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Saturated fat is found in fatty meat, butter, palm and coconut oil, cream, cheese, ghee and lard.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Trans fat is found in industrially-produced trans fat and ruminant trans fat.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: No more than 10% of total energy intake should come from saturated fat.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: No more than 1% of total energy from trans fat of any type.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Lower intakes of saturated and trans fat may have additional health benefits.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Saturated and trans fat can be replaced with polyunsaturated fat or monounsaturated fat from plant sources.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Saturated fat can also be replaced by carbohydrates from foods containing naturally-occurring dietary fibre, such as whole grains, fruits, vegetables and pulses.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Industrially-produced trans fats are not part of a healthy diet and should be avoided.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Fat intake can be reduced by steaming or boiling instead of frying, and replacing butter, lard, and ghee with oils rich in polyunsaturated fat.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Eating reduced-fat dairy foods and lean meats, or trimming visible fat from meat is recommended.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Limiting the consumption of baked and fried foods, and pre-packaged snacks and foods that contain industrially-produced trans fat is advisable.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree
